note: The harness's rebuild plan (register decision 224): after restoring a mutant, rebuild what it built, less what the next mutant builds itself. Each mutant breaks rebuild_plan one way and is judged by its self-test. Since M1-109 (register decision 392) a Python mutant names no build target, and the harness builds nothing for it; until then every mutant named orbsim_shaders as a no-op, which made every shader an input of this file. The last mutant stops the main loop using the plan at all; the self-test cannot see the loop, so it survives here, declared -- it is caught by running m1-95.json, which every full rerun does.

mutants.name: the next mutant's own targets are rebuilt first as well
mutants.find: plan.append([t for t in dict.fromkeys(built_by(previous)) if t not in own])

mutants.name: nothing is rebuilt after a restore
mutants.find: plan.append([t for t in dict.fromkeys(built_by(previous)) if t not in own])

mutants.name: a mutant's suites are not counted as built by it
the two neighbours are swapped
mutants.find: for previous, following in zip(mutants, mutants[1:]):
mutants.replace: for following, previous in zip(mutants, mutants[1:]):

mutants.name: the plan is shifted by one mutant
the main loop ignores the plan
mutants.why: The self-test judges rebuild_plan, not the loop that uses it. This fault is M1-95's own, and m1-95.json is its test: run with this mutant, its comment-only mutant is judged against a stale test_math and caught, so that file fails. Every full rerun runs m1-95.json. A nested pass as a ctest judge was not added, because check would then run a mutation pass. Declared 2026-09-28 under decision 224.
